sources.title: Barbados Parliament: Cultural Industries Development Act, 2013 (amended copy)
sources.said: “approved producer of audio-visual content” or “approved producer ” means a film production company incorporated under the Companies Act, … (c) media - broadcast media including television, radio and cable, digital media including software and computer services, film and video, … (3) Where an approved producer referred to in subsection (1) has in an income year incurred expenditure for the purpose of the production and acquisition in respect of local films, then in calculating the assessable income of the approved producer for an income year, there shall be a write-off of 100 per cent.

sources.title: National Cultural Foundation: Cultural Industries Development Fund
sources.said: The Cultural Industries Development Fund is open to all citizens of Barbados and companies registered in Barbados whose principal shareholder or partner is a citizen of the island. … Creative entrepreneurs are limited to one grant disbursement within a 12-month period and one disbursement per cultural project. … Project Execution funding is provided to creative entrepreneurs seeking assistance to complete a cultural or creative project that provides opportunities to market, promote and showcase the cultural product or service or to generate revenue through the sale of artistic or creative work. (Up to $30,000)

figures.finding: Part VII speaks of 'audio-visual content' and 'local films'; television is a cultural industry under s.2, but the Act names no series terms. A tax deduction, not a credit: what it is worth depends on the producer's income and rate, which the game would need from Barbados's income tax.

figures.finding: Deductions against income, not a credit on cost; the investor deduction ran five years from commencement (proclaimed 2015 per producer-BB.json), so it may have lapsed.

value.investorDeduction: 100% of the investment, first five years from commencement
value.appliesTo: approved cultural projects, the performing arts included

sources.said: (a) arts and culture - the performing arts, visual arts, literary arts, … Where in an income year a cultural entrepreneur, cultural practitioner or a governmental entity incurs expenditure in respect of an artistic work, however defined, there shall be allowed as a deduction, in ascertaining the chargeable profit derived from the cultural activities of the cultural entrepreneur, cultural practitioner or the governmental entity for that year of income, an allowance equal to 150 per cent of the actual expenditure up to a maximum of $250 000. … (2) The deduction referred to in subsection (1) may only be claimed in respect of the initial acquisition of the work and where the work is done by a resident of Barbados. … there shall be deducted an amount equal to 150 per cent of the expenditure incurred. … Where an investor makes an investment in a cultural practitioner or approved cultural project, in calculating the assessable income of the investor there shall be deducted an amount equal to 100 per cent from their assessable income for the first five years from the commencement of this Act.
